mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 5 Series 550i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt engine for a BMW 550i typically costs £4,500-£9,000 supply-only depending on the generation and engine code. Used units start from £1,500, reconditioned from £3,438. Fitting adds approximately 16-22 hours of labour at specialist rates.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW F10 550i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N63 engine in the F10 550i (2010-2016) is prone to timing chain guide failure. Warning signs include a rattling or whining noise from the front of the engine on startup or under acceleration. Catastrophic failure can occur without warning.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW E60 550i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The E60 550i (2005-2010) is a modern classic with a loyal following, but N62 valve stem seal failure is almost inevitable. A well-maintained E60 550i is worth £3,000-£8,000. If the car is solid and the replacement cost makes financial sense, many owners choose to invest.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 550i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 550i engine replacement takes 2-4 days for a specialist workshop, including removal, fitting, and testing. Supply-only delivery is usually 1-3 working days. Complexity is high - N63 V8 work is labour-intensive.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 550i engines across generations?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 550i badge has covered three main engine variants: the N62B48 4.8-litre naturally aspirated V8 with 367hp (E60/E61, 2005-2010), the N63B44O0 4.4-litre twin-turbo V8 with 407hp (F10, 2010-2013), and the N63B44T0 4.4-litre twin-turbo V8 with 445hp (F10 LCI, 2013-2016).

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a BMW 550i replacement engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every rebuilt or reconditioned BMW 550i engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Some suppliers offer extended coverage on premium rebuilds. Always confirm exact terms with your chosen supplier.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 5 Series 550i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 550i debuted in 2005 as the flagship petrol V8 of the E60 5 Series range, delivering effortless performance and genuine executive-car prestige. Over two generations - the E60/E61 and the F10 - the 550i has been powered by BMW's 4.4-litre and 4.8-litre V8 engines, evolving from the naturally aspirated N62 to the twin-turbocharged N63 family.

milestones.description: **2005** - E60/E61 550i launched with N62B48 4.8-litre naturally aspirated V8, 367hp, 490Nm torque
**2005-2010** - N62B48 produced across E60/E61 550i, E63/E64 650i and E70 X5 4.8i applications
**2010** - F10 550i launched with N63B44O0 4.4-litre twin-turbo V8, 407hp, 600Nm
**2013** - F10 LCI 550i receives updated N63B44T0 engine with improved 445hp output
**2016** - F10/F11 550i production ends; replaced by G30 540i

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 5 Series 550i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 5 Series 550i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 550i's V8 engines are among the most complex and expensive to maintain in the 5 Series range. Both the N62 and N63 families suffer from well-documented, often catastrophic failures that can make replacement the only sensible option. Rebuilt 550i engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: N63 Timing Chain Failure - Why the BMW 5 Series F10 550i Fails Catastrophically
problems.rootCause: The N63's timing chain guides are made of brittle plastic that breaks apart with age and heat. When guides fail, the chain can slacken or snap, causing piston-to-valve contact and catastrophic internal damage. The hot-V turbo configuration creates extreme under-bonnet temperatures that accelerate component wear.

repairOptions.longevity: Early intervention if rattle is heard; significantly cheaper than full replacement

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New valve stem seals, often part of Customer Care Package
repairOptions.longevity: Addresses oil consumption and smoke on startup
When chain has failed or internal damage has occurred

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical F10 550i (2010-2016) is worth roughly £5,000-£15,000 depending on condition, mileage and specification. If you're facing a full rebuilt engine at £6,500-£9,000 plus fitting, the replacement cost may approach or exceed 60% of a lower-value F10's market value. Many owners choose to scrap their 550i rather than rebuild an engine that might fail again.
problems.recommendation: If your F10 550i's N63 engine makes a rattling noise on startup, have the timing chain inspected immediately - catching it early can save the engine. However, be aware that even with preventative work, the N63's reputation for recurring issues means replacement is often the only permanent solution. A rebuilt engine with upgraded components and warranty offers the best chance of long-term reliability.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N63B44 BMW 5 Series 550i engine prices

problems.h4: N62 Valve Stem Seal Failure - Smoke and Oil Consumption in the BMW 5 Series E60 550i
problems.rootCause: The N62's valve stem seals harden and lose their sealing ability with age and heat. This allows oil to leak past the valve guides into the combustion chamber, causing blue smoke on startup and after idling. The CCV (crankcase ventilation) system can also fail, exacerbating oil consumption.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New valve stem seals, valve cover gaskets
New CCV valve, breather hoses, valve cover service
repairOptions.longevity: If oil consumption is caused by CCV failure
When oil consumption is severe or other failures have occurred

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical E60 550i (2005-2010) is worth roughly £3,000-£8,000 depending on condition. Valve stem seal replacement at £2,500-£4,500 is a significant investment but often worthwhile for a well-maintained example. If the car has other issues, evaluate scrap value first.
problems.recommendation: Valve stem seal failure is almost inevitable on high-mileage N62 engines. If you notice blue smoke on startup, have the seals inspected. Catching the issue early and replacing the seals with upgraded components can restore the engine to good health. However, if the oil consumption is severe or the engine has other problems, a rebuilt unit may be more cost-effective.

problems.h4: N63 Turbocharger & HPFP Failure - Power Loss in the BMW 5 Series F10 550i
problems.rootCause: The N63's hot-V turbocharger configuration exposes turbos to extreme heat, leading to oil coking, wastegate rattle and eventual failure. The high-pressure fuel pump can fail, dumping raw fuel into cylinders and destroying pistons and rods. Injector failure is also common.

repairOptions.longevity: If wastegate rattle or loss of power is noticed
If fuel system failure has occurred
When turbo or fuel system failure has caused internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Same as above - F10 550i values typically £5,000-£15,000. Turbocharger replacement at £2,500-£4,000 is often viable if the rest of the engine is sound. However, if the failure has caused internal damage, replacement may be the only option.
problems.recommendation: If you notice a loss of power, excessive exhaust smoke or a rattling noise from the turbos, have the system inspected promptly. N63 turbo and fuel system failures are well-documented. A specialist who understands the N63's unique challenges is essential. For cars with high mileage or multiple issues, a fully rebuilt engine with upgraded components and warranty offers the best value.
